core_summary: Provides an in-depth analysis of market structures, price equilibrium mechanics, supply chain management, and consumer protection. Examines physical markets (haats, mandis, malls) versus online aggregators, the Surat textile supply chain case study, government interventions (MRP, MSP, ceiling/floor prices), and product quality certification standards.
key_concepts: Price Equilibrium Mechanics: The interaction of buyer demand and seller supply establishing a mutually agreed price where market shortages or surpluses are resolved.
Physical vs Digital Supply Chains: The multi-tiered movement of goods through producers, wholesalers, cold storages, distributors, and retailers versus direct e-commerce fulfillment.
Government Price Controls: State market intervention using Minimum Support Prices (MSP) to safeguard producer incomes and Maximum Retail Prices (MRP) to protect consumers.
Intermediary Value Addition: The essential role played by wholesalers and retailers in absorbing storage risk, bulk breaking, transport logistics, and localized consumer access.
Consumer Quality Standard Verification: Utilizing government logos (FSSAI, ISI, AGMARK, BEE Stars) and packaging label audits to ensure food safety and product honesty.

key_terms.definition: The market price where the quantity of goods supplied by producers equals the quantity demanded by consumers.
The entire network of entities, assets, information, and activities involved in creating and delivering a product from raw material to final buyer.
An intermediary entity that purchases goods in large quantities from manufacturers and resells them in smaller lots to retailers.
The maximum price calculated and printed on a product package that can legally be charged to a consumer in India.
Food Safety and Standards Authority of India; the statutory body governing food quality, licensing, and safety standards.

key_takeaways: Prices in competitive markets are determined by the dynamic balance between consumer demand and producer supply.
Supply chains involve multiple specialized intermediaries who bridge geographical and logistical gaps between factories/farms and final consumers.
Government regulatory standards and certification marks (FSSAI, ISI, AGMARK) protect consumers against price gouging, adulteration, and unsafe products.
